commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that plants only respire at night.

fixIt.corrected: Plants respire around the clock: at night there is simply no photosynthesis to hide it.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: state when plants respire, and why respiration looks switched off by day.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks the statement that plants only respire at night.

fixIt.corrected: Plants respire around the clock, day and night: respiration never stops - photosynthesis just masks it by day.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence what the respiration dot keeps doing in scene s6 after the sun is replaced by the moon.

modelAnswers.answer: The folds give a huge surface area for respiratory enzymes, so more aerobic respiration and more ATP production can happen.
modelAnswers.question: Explain why the folded cristae of a mitochondrion help it make more ATP.

modelAnswers.answer: Yeast: ethanol + carbon dioxide. Muscle: lactic acid. Both yield far less ATP than aerobic respiration because glucose is only partly broken down.
modelAnswers.question: Compare anaerobic respiration in yeast and in muscle: name the products of each and state the ATP yield compared with aerobic respiration.

nextSteps: Reteach the plant-respiration trap from the paired notes trap before any further energetics work: plants respire around the clock, day and night.
Practise the anaerobic comparison from scene s4, checking each product against its pathway and the ATP yield against aerobic respiration.
strengths: Most of the class can state the aerobic respiration equation, glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy, with about 32 ATP per glucose.
The class can explain why folded cristae help a mitochondrion make more ATP.
